tertius.title: Tertius: The NT Greek Vocab Trainer App

settings.editor:
We at LatinPerDiem are pleased to announce Tertius: The NT Greek Vocab Trainer, an app that gets you ready to read the New Testament in Greek. If you learned some Koine or Attic Greek once and want to read the New Testament without reaching for the English, Tertius builds the vocabulary that stands between you and the text.

Developed by Dr. David C. Noe and the LatinPerDiem team, Tertius brings the words of the New Testament to your phone, tablet, or computer. Since 2015, LatinPerDiem has delivered manageable, context-rich Latin and Greek lessons to a worldwide audience through its YouTube channel (now more than 2,500 free videos). Our philosophy is simple: people learn languages best through real use in context rather than isolated abstractions.

Learn the Words the New Testament Actually Uses

Tertius teaches the 1,287 words of Bruce Metzger's Lexical Aids for Students of New Testament Greek, most frequent first, with each word's root family woven in, so a new word is learned alongside the words from which it is built. As you master words, Tertius shows how much of the New Testament you now know: the share of all the running words in the text covered by the words you have learned. The 28 commonest words already cover half of the New Testament.

Features

  • Metzger's 1,287 New Testament words, ordered by frequency, with root families woven in
  • A session-based memory system: a word is mastered once you answer it correctly on the first try in five sessions on five different days, and mastered words come back at growing intervals for review
  • Metzger's glosses, with his English derivatives as memory aids for 441 words ("Cf. apostasy")
  • Souter's Pocket Lexicon to the Greek New Testament built in, searchable in Greek letters, Latin letters, or English
  • MossMethod meanings: if you have studied MossMethod for Greek, Tertius shows Moss's meaning for the 625 words in his First Greek Reader and counts them toward your progress
  • Readings beyond the New Testament: eleven passages with H. P. V. Nunn's notes, chiefly early Christian (the Didache, Hermas, Clement, the martyrdoms of Polycarp and Ignatius, Diognetus), with Plato and Lucian besides, coloured by what you have mastered, every word tappable, and a public-domain English translation one tap away
  • Diacriticals that change meaning: a quiz on 18 sets of words spelled alike but for an accent or breathing (εἰ and εἶ, ἤ and ἥ, οὐ and οὗ), each in a verse of the New Testament
  • Your choice of pace (3, 5, 8, or 12 new words per session), answer mode (recall or multiple choice), and direction (Greek to English, English to Greek, or both)
  • Share your progress with a study partner or group [CONFIRM WHAT SHIPS AT LAUNCH]
  • Works offline; iOS, Android, and the web [CONFIRM PLATFORMS]

Getting the Most from the App

  • Train daily. About 30 minutes per day, five days per week. Several short sessions fit in that time.
  • Recall before you look. After a first look at a new word, Tertius asks for its meaning before showing it. Retrieving a word from memory fixes it far better than looking at it again.
  • Watch the share of the New Testament. At 80%, you know the words behind eight of every ten words in the text, and daily reading of the Greek New Testament becomes realistic.
  • Then read. The point of Tertius is to get you into the text. Join The Greek New Testament in a Year, or start Matthew 1 on your own.

Read the Whole Greek New Testament with Us

Tertius launches with The Greek New Testament in a Year, an exclusive reading group led by Dr. Noe for 50 founding members. We train together in Tertius for six to eight weeks, then read the whole New Testament in Greek, about 30 verses per day, Monday to Friday, in small squads with a weekly live hour. Founding members get exclusive early access to Tertius, and lifetime access free. Learn more and join a squad.

Whom It's For

Tertius is built for readers who already know some Greek: pastors and seminary graduates whose Greek has rusted, seminary students, MossMethod students and graduates, teachers, and lifelong learners who want to read the New Testament in the original. True beginners should start with a first-year course, such as MossMethod for Greek.

Credits

David Noe (project supervisor, word data review) · Kenneth Jackson (programmer) · [OTHERS]

Sources: Bruce M. Metzger, Lexical Aids for Students of New Testament Greek (1946); Alexander Souter, A Pocket Lexicon to the Greek New Testament (1916); Charles Melville Moss, A First Greek Reader (1893), Vocabulary; H. P. V. Nunn, A Short Syntax of New Testament Greek (1920), Appendix II; the SBL Greek New Testament, via MorphGNT (CC BY-SA 3.0); English translations by Kirsopp Lake, Marcus Dods, E. C. E. Owen, Harold North Fowler, and H. W. and F. G. Fowler.

Tertius comes free with membership in The Greek New Testament in a Year; afterward you can download it for a one-time $9.99. [STORE LINKS AT LAUNCH] Questions? Contact us at info@latinperdiem.com.

settings.editor:
Read the whole Greek New Testament in a year via Tertius, with Dr. David Noe.

An exclusive reading group: fifty places, about thirty verses per day, all twenty-seven books.

$249 one-time · [PLACES COUNTER: "N of 50 places left"] · Sign-up is open until the places are filled.

Join a squad →

I, Tertius

Near the end of Romans, after Paul's long list of greetings, another voice breaks in: ἀσπάζομαι ὑμᾶς ἐγὼ Τέρτιος ὁ γράψας τὴν ἐπιστολὴν ἐν κυρίῳ (Rom. 16:22). [DAVID'S TRANSLATION]

Tertius was the scribe who wrote the letter down. Paul often worked this way: he dictated, and at the end took the pen to add a greeting in his own hand (1 Cor. 16:21; Gal. 6:11; Col. 4:18; 2 Thess. 3:17). Every word of Romans passed through Tertius's ear and onto his page, in Greek, before anyone in Rome read a line of it.

Tertius wrote out one book of the New Testament. In a year, you will read all twenty-seven.

How It Works

1. Train in Tertius (6–8 weeks). Every founding member gets exclusive early access to Tertius: The NT Greek Vocab Trainer, our new app for the vocabulary of the New Testament. About 30 minutes per day, five days per week, brings back the words you once knew and adds the ones you never learned. When Tertius shows you know 80% of the New Testament's running words (about 370 words), you are ready to read. Anyone who needs longer keeps training and joins the reading as soon as they pass.

2. The year of reading (52 weeks). From Matthew 1 to Revelation 22, in canonical order: about 30 verses per day, Monday to Friday, with weekends for rest or catch-up.

  • Weekly live session (one hour on Zoom, recorded) [DAY AND TIME TBD]: Dr. Noe reads the opening of the week's passage aloud and translates it, then takes your questions.
  • Squad letter every Monday morning: progress, a verse of the week, and encouragement.
  • Your squad: ten readers and a volunteer captain, named for one of Paul's co-workers. Squad Barnabas, Squad Priscilla, Squad Timothy, Squad Phoebe, Squad Silas.
  • Milestones at the end of Matthew, the four Gospels, Acts, Romans, Paul's letters, Hebrews and the general letters, and Revelation.

What You Get

  • Exclusive early access to Tertius: The NT Greek Vocab Trainer, and lifetime access free
  • A place in a squad of ten, with a captain
  • An exclusive weekly one-hour live session with Dr. Noe on Zoom, recorded for anyone who misses one
  • The Monday squad letter for the whole program
  • A completion certificate and your name on the roll of honor
  • Continuing education credit [CONFIRM: hours, and how teachers claim it]
  • An exclusive say in the app: founding members are Tertius's first testers, and your feedback shapes it

Whom It's For

Pastors and seminary graduates whose Greek has rusted: you learned it once, you preach from the English, and you would like to read the New Testament in Greek again. Teachers and lifelong learners with a year of Greek behind them are welcome too.

What You Need

  • Some Greek. One year of Koine or Attic, however long ago. Exceptions are possible with the instructor's approval: write to us. Tertius teaches vocabulary, not the alphabet and basic grammar. New to Greek? Start with MossMethod for Greek.
  • The text: the SBL Greek New Testament (SBLGNT), free to read online and available in print.
  • A lexicon: BDAG is recommended, not required. Tertius has Metzger's glosses and Souter's Pocket Lexicon built in.
  • The time: about 30 minutes per day while training; 30 minutes to an hour per day while reading.
  • A phone, tablet, or computer for Tertius [CONFIRM PLATFORMS].

Timeline

We begin in January 2027, alongside Homer's Hecatomb [CONFIRM DATE]: six to eight weeks of training in Tertius, then fifty-two weeks of reading, about sixty weeks from first drill to the last verse of Revelation.

Questions

Is $249 the whole cost? Yes, one time. It includes Tertius, which will later be a one-time $9.99 download. You will want your own copy of the SBLGNT, and BDAG if you have it.

What if the 50 places are gone? Join the waitlist for the second group.

What if I miss a week? Catch up on weekends, or watch the recorded session. Your captain will help.

My Greek is from seminary, twenty years ago. Is that enough? Yes. That is whom the program is for. The training weeks in Tertius are there to bring it back.

Do teachers get continuing education credit? Yes. [CONFIRM DETAILS]

Can I be a squad captain? Yes. Say so on the welcome questionnaire after you sign up. [CAPTAIN DESCRIPTION LINK]

Refunds? No. All sales are final.

Join a squad →

Questions? Contact us at info@latinperdiem.com.
